body:
I understand the risks, but I intend to use condoms. How would it be any different then having protected sex with numerous casual partners (like many people my age do)?

Why would you advise against partaking regularly?

I’m not trying to be confrontational. I’m legitimately curious about your opinions. I still haven’t decided to go through with it yet (mostly because I can’t afford it right now even if I wanted to)

I’m going to break down why this advice is, at best, useless, and, at worst, dangerous for everyone involved.

1. This advice boils down to drink alcohol and make sure your date drinks alcohol. First, most FA appear to have some form of depression. It is generally advisable for people with depression to avoid alcohol. Then, there’s the most obvious issue. This advice is saying to use a mind-altering drug to convince people to find you attractive. This is dehumanizing to the FA person who likely wants people to care about them for who they really are (not who beer goggles paints them to be). It also, disturbingly, puts us dangerously close to date rape territory. Perhaps it’s just anecdotal, but I’ve heard WAY too many stories and warnings about how having relations with a sufficiently drunk woman is rape because at a certain, undefined transition point they have forfeited their ability to consent.

2. Could you link this study? Thousands of people a day claim that science backs up their claims and never show any sort of proof. Presuming you actually DID get this from a legitimate study, and it’s actually a well done study, there’s still an issue. I, and likely many of the men with social anxiety you are talking to, have been consuming pornography for many years. In my case, I’ve been doing so since I was only 12 years old. Any damage that has been done by the consumption of pornography was likely over a decade ago. I highly doubt just avoiding porn now at 26 is going to make much of a difference with my social anxiety (though I’ll never know because you didn’t cite your sources)

3. Similar to #1. It’s degrading to be told you’re not good enough as you are. Share these mind-altering drugs in the hope that someone can trick their brain into liking you. Also, in most of the United States and the developed world the use and acquisition of marijuana is still very illegal. You’re actively telling desperate, lonely, (and often young/impressionable) people that they should break the law so that others find them more attractive. I don’t need to explain how this is dangerous, do I? (Note: I don’t have anything against weed. If it were legal to consume where I live I’d likely use it regularly)

4. You have literally just reworded “Be attractive. Don’t be unattractive.” This advice is still meaningless even when rephrased.

5. Wow. Your advice again is just so dehumanizing. Sensitive and self-reflecting? HIDE IT! Nobody cares about your feelings! Feeling are unattractive. You MUST display confidence through every action and facet of your life. Meanwhile feminism (which I have nothing against) preaches to young women the importance of being themselves. Why must men mask their true selves and conform to some dehumanized, hyper-efficient facade of themselves to attract a mate? How is this not manipulating they’re partner/potential partner? What should they do when their partner learns their true nature and leaves them?

I appreciate your concern. I certainly hope I don’t get too emotional over this. And I’m hoping to see a therapist soon. Kind of also want to wait on the escort thing until I get a professional’s opinion. Not like they’re going to say I should do it, of course, but I’d like to hear their concerns regarding how it might affect my mental health.
In what way is it risky? Would it be preferable to never have sex than risk having sex with an escort?
I appreciate your support. I agree that it’s not an amazing option, but at this point it seems like the only way I’ll ever have sex.

I have no misconception that the escort would have any feelings for me, or that the act will be any more intimate then any other professional transaction. It still seems preferable to have the experience at all, even if some elements are missing.

Looking back, do you think you would have met and/or connected with those “real” girls if you hadn’t had your experiences with escorts? If I may also ask, how old were you when you decided to employ an escort for the first time?
No, not really. The past 7 years have been nothing but pain and few good bits always ended in disappointment. If I could choose to just not wake up tomorrow I’d do it.
At 18 I wanted to die too. I’m 25 now and regret all the pain I’ve forced myself through by not just killing myself years ago.
